state.incidentInput: Payments team says their latency went up around 14:00. Is payments broken?
state.summary: Payments is not the cause. CFG-502 (inventory DB_POOL_MAX 20->80 at 13:52) over-committed orders-db (610 potential vs 400 max); inventory holds ~320 connections (LOG-076, LOG-121), starving orders-service ("too many clients"), causing checkout errors. Payments latency is a secondary effect of checkout retries (LOG-046); the rollback DEP-103 was a red herring and the 5xx alert persists after it (ALR-014).
state.impact: Onset 13:55. Checkout errors up to 7.9%, p99 5s, orders errors 10% (MET-checkout.error_rate_pct, MET-orders.error_rate_pct). CUST-001: 87 tickets by 14:30; CUST-002: 14 charged without confirmation. Search/browse unaffected (CUST-004).

timeline.note: Deploy payments-service v2.14.0: Add 3DS2 challenge flow for EU cards; bump HTTP client library to 5.2

ERROR orders-service: FATAL: sorry, too many clients already
Spike in "Something went wrong" at Place Order. 87 tickets by 14:30 (normal: ~5/hour).
WARN payments-service: inbound request queue depth 42 (client checkout-service retries)
LOG orders-db: connections: inventory_svc=318 orders_svc=64 reporting_svc=12 superuser=3 total=397/400
Config checkout-service (feature-flag-service, by pshah): flag payments_retry_on_timeout: true -> false
Rollback payments-service v2.13.4: Rollback v2.14.0 during INC-2213 investigation
[critical] checkout-service 5xx rate above 2% (still firing after payments rollback) (7.4%)

hypotheses.statement: CFG-502 raised inventory pool to 80 x6 replicas, exhausting orders-db connections; orders-service can't get connections, checkout fails.
hypotheses.reasoning: Onset 13:55 right after config; inventory holds 318-320 of 397 connections; orders pool starved; errors persist after payments rollback. Payments latency from checkout retries into it, eased when CFG-504 disabled retries.
Payments error rate and processor latency unchanged; checkout errors continued after rollback.

openQuestions: Did the inventory owner intend CFG-502, and why? (inventory on-call)

nextActions.action: Tell payments team their latency was a downstream effect of checkout retries, not a payments fault
Reconcile the 14 'charged but no confirmation' orders and holds
Add PgBouncer and a connection-budget guardrail on pool changes (INC-2041 item open)

state.stakeholderUpdate: Customers are seeing failures when placing orders since about 14:00. Payments is not broken; its slowness was a side effect. The likely cause is a configuration change that let the inventory service take most of the shared database's connections, leaving the orders service starved. We are reverting that setting and will check the 14 orders where a card was charged without confirmation. Next update in 30 minutes.

similarIncidents.similarity: Resembles H1 (active). Orders failing, orders-db connection exhaustion: reporting-service raised its DB pool from 15 to 100 to speed up a quarterly report.
similarIncidents.lesson: 30 minutes lost investigating the most recent deploy rather than recent config changes.

similarIncidents.similarity: Resembles H2 (rejected). Checkout 500s after payments deploy: payments-service v2.9.0 shipped a serialization bug for a new card-network field.
similarIncidents.lesson: payments-service's own error rate jumped from 0.2% to 12% within 2 minutes of the 100% rollout.
